user_input: Compare AA24-109A and AA23-352A: which actors are reported using Mimikatz, and how do their advisory software-to-technique mappings compare? Cite both reports and keep each mapping within its source context.
response:
LockBit affiliates use Mimikatz. [E1, E2, E3, E4]
Volt Typhoon actors use Mimikatz to harvest credentials. [E5, E6]
Phobos actors use Mimikatz to export credentials. [E8, E9, E10, E11]
Akira threat actors use Mimikatz to dump credentials. [E12, E13, E14, E15]
Black Basta affiliates use Mimikatz for privilege escalation. [E16, E17, E18, E19]
Medusa actors use Mimikatz to access credential material. [E20, E21, E22, E23]
LockBit and Phobos actors use Mimikatz for defense evasion. [E4, E11]
Volt Typhoon actors use Impacket in addition to Mimikatz. [E5, E6]

reference: AA24-109A reports Akira threat actors using Mimikatz, with advisory mappings T1003; AA23-352A reports Play ransomware actors using Mimikatz, with advisory mappings T1003. These mappings describe the cited reports and do not establish that every use of the software has these behaviors. Both reports cite the same parent technique, T1003 (OS Credential Dumping), for their reported Mimikatz use.
